title: Mock 3 · Pricing & Hedging
blurb: Fair value, hedge ratios, Greeks, strangles and protective puts, plus clearing basics.

questions.q: Exchange-traded derivatives started in India with trading in index futures on Nifty and Sensex in:
questions.explanation: Index futures on Nifty and Sensex commenced in June 2000. Index options followed in June 2001, stock options in July 2001 and stock futures in November 2001.
hints: June 2001 was when index options started.
Correct: June 2000.
November 2001 was when stock futures started.
July 2001 was when stock options started.

questions.q: According to the workbook, derivatives markets enable the transfer of risk:
options: From those exposed to risk with a low risk appetite to participants with a high risk appetite
From participants with a high risk appetite to those with a low risk appetite
From the exchange to the clearing corporation
questions.explanation: Derivatives transfer risk from those who are exposed but risk-averse (hedgers) to those willing to take risk (traders).
hints: Correct: hedgers pass risk to risk-takers.
This reverses the direction.
This is not the economic function described.
Brokers do not absorb client market risk.

questions.q: A market-cap weighted index was set at 1,000 when the constituents' total market cap was ₹2,300 crore. The market cap is now ₹2,580 crore. What is the current index value?
questions.explanation: Index = current market cap / base market cap × base value = 2,580 / 2,300 × 1,000 = 1,121.74.
hints: You added the ₹280 crore change straight to the base value.
The ratio is inverted.
Arithmetic slip.

questions.q: An index is at 20,000. The financing cost is 10% p.a. and the dividend yield is 2% p.a. Using F = S(1 + r − q)^T, what is the fair price of a 90-day futures contract?
hints: This applies only 2% simple interest; you need the net carry for 90 days.
This uses simple interest (1 + 0.08 × 90/365), not the workbook's compounded formula.
This ignores the dividend yield (uses 10% only).

questions.q: You hold an equity portfolio worth ₹1.5 crore with a beta of 1.2. Nifty futures trade at 25,000 with a lot size of 75. To hedge, you should:
questions.explanation: N = (1,50,00,000 × 1.2) / (25,000 × 75) = 1,80,00,000 / 18,75,000 = 9.6 ≈ 10. To protect against a fall, you sell (short) index futures.
hints: This ignores beta (1.5 cr / 18.75 lakh = 8).
Correct: 9.6, rounded to 10, short.
Buying futures adds to the risk instead of hedging it.
This over-hedges; recompute with the futures value per lot.

questions.q: On August 5, an investor decides to sell his portfolio on September 12 and wants to hedge with index futures. Following the workbook's thumb rule, he should short the:
options: A mix of August and September contracts
questions.explanation: Choose the contract that expires just after the date you wish to unwind. September futures (expiring at the end of September) expire just after September 12.
hints: August expires before the planned exit date.
October works but is not the contract expiring 'just after' the exit date.
There is no need to split across months.
Correct: the September contract expires just after September 12.

questions.q: If a stock's futures price is higher than its fair (theoretical) price, an arbitrageur would:
options: Buy futures and sell the stock in the cash market
Buy the stock in the cash market and sell futures
Buy both the stock and the futures
Sell both the stock and the futures
questions.explanation: Overpriced futures trigger cash-and-carry arbitrage: buy (long) in the cash market, sell (short) the futures, and carry to expiry.
hints: That is reverse cash-and-carry, used when futures are underpriced.
Correct: cash-and-carry arbitrage.
This is not a hedged arbitrage.
This is not a hedged arbitrage.

questions.q: The daily settlement price of an equity futures contract is computed as:
options: The closing price of the underlying in the cash market
The opening price of the futures contract
The volume-weighted average price of the futures contract in the last half hour
The highest traded price of the day
questions.explanation: Daily settlement price = volume-weighted average price of the futures contract during the last 30 minutes. The FINAL settlement price uses the underlying's closing price on expiry.
hints: The underlying's closing price is used for the FINAL settlement price on expiry.
The opening price is not used for settlement.
Correct: the last 30-minute VWAP of the futures contract.
The high is not used for settlement.

questions.q: You buy a 1,500-strike put at ₹45 (lot size 400). At expiry the stock settles at ₹1,420. What is your net profit?
hints: This ignores the premium paid.
This is only the premium outflow (45 × 400).
The put is in the money, so the position is in profit.

questions.q: A call has a delta of 0.45 and a gamma of 0.05. If the underlying rises by ₹2, the new delta will be approximately:
questions.explanation: Gamma is the change in delta per ₹1 change. New delta = 0.45 + 0.05 × 2 = 0.55.
hints: This applies gamma for a ₹1 move only.
This adds 0.02 instead of 0.10.
This doubles delta, which is not how gamma works.

questions.q: An option has a theta of 2.5 (per day). Other things remaining equal, by roughly how much will its premium fall over the next 4 days?
questions.explanation: Theta is the premium decline per day of time decay: 2.5 × 4 = ₹10.
hints: That is the decay for one day only.
You added 4 to 2.5 instead of multiplying.
You divided by 4 instead of multiplying.

questions.q: With other factors constant, an increase in which of the following raises the value of a call but lowers the value of a put?
questions.explanation: High interest rates increase call values and decrease put values. Volatility and time raise both; a higher strike lowers calls and raises puts.
hints: Volatility raises both calls and puts.
Time to expiry raises both calls and puts.
A higher strike LOWERS calls and RAISES puts, the opposite effect.
Correct: higher interest rates mean calls up, puts down.

questions.q: In exchange-traded options, who is required to deposit margin with the exchange?
questions.explanation: The buyer's maximum loss is the premium already paid, so no margin is needed. The writer has an obligation and potentially unlimited loss, so the writer pays margin and MTM.
hints: The buyer pays the premium, not margin.
Correct: only the writer pays margin.
In futures both pay margin; in options only the writer does.
The writer must pay margin.

questions.q: A trader buys a 900-strike put at ₹12 and a 1,000-strike call at ₹15 (same expiry). What are the break-even points?
questions.explanation: Long strangle: total premium = 27. Lower BEP = 900 − 27 = 873; upper BEP = 1,000 + 27 = 1,027.
hints: This uses only one leg's premium on each side.
This uses only one leg's premium on each side.
These are the strikes; between them the trader loses the full ₹27.

questions.q: An investor buys a stock at ₹800 and buys a 780-strike put at ₹12. What is the maximum possible loss per share on this protective put?
questions.explanation: Maximum loss = (stock cost − strike) + put premium = (800 − 780) + 12 = ₹32. Below 780 the put offsets further losses.
hints: This counts only the premium; the strike is below the purchase price.
This counts only the gap between price and strike.
The put caps the loss; it cannot be this large.

questions.q: A trader is short 20 lots of call options with a delta of 0.40. The futures lot size equals the option lot size. To make the position delta-neutral, he should:
questions.explanation: Position delta = −0.40 × 20 = −8 lots. A futures contract has a delta of about 1, so buying 8 lots of futures makes the net delta zero.
hints: Correct: buy 8 lots to offset delta −8.
Selling adds more negative delta.
This ignores the option's delta.
You divided by delta instead of multiplying.

questions.q: A clearing member who is also a trading member and may clear and settle only his own proprietary and clients' trades, but not those of other trading members, is a:
questions.explanation: A Self Clearing Member clears only its own and its clients' trades. A Trading-cum-CM can also clear for other TMs, and a PCM is not a TM at all.
hints: A PCM is not a trading member.
A TCM can clear for other TMs too.
Correct: Self Clearing Member.
A custodial participant is a type of client, not a clearing member.

questions.q: A stock undergoes a split in the ratio 5:1 (adjustment factor A/B). Before the split, a stock option has a strike of ₹2,500 and a market lot of 250. What are the adjusted strike and lot?
questions.explanation: AF = A/B = 5. New strike = 2,500 / 5 = ₹500; new lot = 250 × 5 = 1,250. The contract value is unchanged (₹6,25,000).
hints: Correct: strike ÷ 5 and lot × 5.
Adjusted in the wrong direction.
The lot must also be multiplied by the AF.
The strike must also be divided by the AF.

questions.q: To prevent erroneous order entry in index futures, the exchange applies an operating range of:
options: No limit; any price is accepted
questions.explanation: There are no price bands in derivatives, but operating ranges are 10% of the base price for index futures and stock futures. Option ranges are delta-based.
hints: Too narrow.
Correct: 10% of the base price.
Too wide.
Orders beyond the operating range reach the exchange as a price freeze.

questions.q: In the Nifty contract, a trading member's proprietary account bought 600 and sold 400. Client A bought 300 and sold 100. Client B bought 100 and sold 400. What is the TM's open position?
questions.explanation: Proprietary is netted: +200. Clients are netted individually and then grossed: A +200, B −300. Long = 200 (pro) + 200 (A) = 400; short = 300 (B).
hints: Client positions are not netted against each other.
Gross buys and sells are not used; net each account first.
This misses the proprietary long of 200.
Correct: long 400, short 300.

questions.q: The minimum net worth required for a clearing member in the F&O segment (clearing for others) is:
questions.explanation: A clearing member needs a net worth of at least ₹300 lakh. A CM who clears only his own deals needs ₹100 lakh. ₹50 lakh is the security deposit.
hints: ₹100 lakh applies to a CM clearing only his own deals.
₹50 lakh is the security deposit / liquid net worth figure.
Correct: ₹300 lakh.
Too high.

questions.q: After a stock enters the F&O ban period (aggregate OI above 95% of MWPL), normal trading resumes only when the aggregate open interest falls to:
questions.explanation: Fresh positions are barred once OI exceeds 95% of MWPL. Normal trading resumes when OI comes down to 80% or below.
hints: Not the threshold.
Correct: 80% or below.
60% is the level at which the alert is displayed.
Not the threshold.

questions.q: Which of the following is a responsibility of the clearing corporation?
questions.explanation: The clearing corporation's duties include collecting margins, ensuring smooth daily clearing and settlement, acting as legal counterparty, monitoring positions, deciding daily settlement prices and keeping client margin records.
hints: Correct: the CC decides daily settlement prices.
Premiums are discovered by the market, not fixed by anyone.
Registration is SEBI's role.
STT rates are set by the Union Budget.

questions.q: At the balance sheet date, a client's 'Mark-to-Market Margin – Equity Index Futures A/c' shows a DEBIT balance (net MTM paid). As per ICAI guidance, the client should:
options: Ignore it until the contract is settled
Credit the amount to profit and loss
Create a provision for anticipated loss by debiting profit and loss
Transfer it to a general reserve
questions.explanation: Under the prudence principle, a provision for anticipated loss equal to the debit balance is created by debiting P&L. A credit balance (anticipated profit) is ignored.
hints: Prudence requires losses to be recognised.
A debit balance indicates a loss, not income.
Correct: provide for the anticipated loss.
Reserves are not used for this.

questions.q: Once SEBI forwards a complaint through SCORES, within how many days must the concerned entity resolve it?
questions.explanation: The entity must resolve the complaint within 21 days of receiving intimation from SEBI under SCORES and upload an Action Taken Report.
hints: Too short.
15 days is the ODR timeline for paying an arbitral award.
Too long.
Correct: 21 days.
